title: playable-screen-20of44
queue_order: One binary (this lane's step-1 commit, merged with origin/master), env-only A/B per title: ON queues with no --env (app default); OFF queues --env with all six vars =0. Scope at first registration: 20 of pm/playable-accepted.tsv's 44 titles whose ISO was present on the Nova's DEVICE_ISO_ROOT (confirmed against /home/justin/hakux-work/hardware/titlepush/listing-nova.txt, Oct-3, cross-checked live at queue time). lane.local's brief addendum (10-10 22:46 PDT) revised this: Capcom vs. SNK 2 EO (43430008) was already on the Nova (listing was stale), and lane.local shuffled the remaining 23 onto the Nova overnight itself (unit lanelocal-shuffle1010b, log /home/justin/hakux-work/lanelocal-scratch/shuffle1010.log), not this lane's grant (memory shuffle-means-onto-the-nova). The log reached 'done; Nova free 33 GB' at 2026-10-10 23:43:58 PDT with all 23 verified and the Nova hold released -- all 44 Playable titles are now Nova-resident, so this registration's scope is now the full 44, blocked_titles empty. 14 of the 44 use their own named route (docs/testing/titles/routes/<name>.route); the other 30 have no route in this tree (checked per-title against targets.toml and the routes directory) and run as a soak to the title screen with --frames-every. Queued in batches of about 10 titles, each batch preceded by its own small pilot per the 30-min device-time gate, HAKUX_RELEASE_PRIO=1.
judge: per-title: logcat read for a crash/hang/abort in ON that OFF does not show (fatal); route-frames or --frames-every captures at matched points, compared by region, ON vs OFF (frames); reportasync1010's armed/late counters where GET_REPORT traffic appears in logcat (reports); both arms' perf_regimen.json/telemetry fps, reported not gated (gfps). No single numeric threshold applies across 20 different titles -- each title's own row is read by eye against its own OFF baseline, recorded in docs/lanes/fastpaths1010/NOTES.md and PR.md's screen table.
baseline: Every one of the 20 titles already has an accepted Playable verdict (pm/playable-accepted.tsv) from an earlier run, most on this same Nova, establishing what correct gameplay for that title's route looks like; this screen's OFF arm is that same known-good code path (all six switches at their native C default, off), and ON is the new default. A title regressing between ON and OFF here would be a regression from fastpaths1010's own step-1 commit, not a pre-existing issue the Playable verdict already accepted.
prediction: None of the 44 fail: reportasync1010, texscan1010 (paired with REPORT_ASYNC), drawrec1010 and perdrawon1010 each already screened their own switch (or pair) on some subset of Playable titles or a broader survey without a correctness regression (texscan1010's own finding was a PERFORMANCE regression when TEXSCAN runs alone, not a correctness one, and this toggle never ships TEXSCAN alone). What would refute it: any ON-only crash/hang; any ON-only visual defect in a frame region OFF does not show; a title whose reportasync counters show armed below 100% that OFF's do not (a GET_REPORT race the other three lanes' own survey titles did not happen to hit).
expect_note: fail_titles starts empty: the claim under test is that no title fails. blocked_titles started as 24 titles not yet on the Nova (this lane's Oct-3/4 listing check was stale by one: Capcom vs. SNK 2 EO was already there). lane.local's addendum (10-10 22:46 PDT) shuffled the remaining 23 onto the Nova overnight (lanelocal-shuffle1010b, log /home/justin/hakux-work/lanelocal-scratch/shuffle1010.log), which reached 'done; Nova free 33 GB' at 2026-10-10 23:43:58 PDT with all 23 verified -- all 44 Playable titles are Nova-resident as of this update, so blocked_titles is now empty and the scope is the full 44. 14 use their own named route (Alien Hominid, KOF: Maximum Impact - Maniax, Azurik: Rise of Perathia, WWE Raw 2, 50 Cent: Bulletproof, Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance, Crimson Skies: High Road to Revenge, Kabuki Warriors, 187: Ride or Die, Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2x, Castlevania: Curse of Darkness, Spikeout: Battle Street, Jet Set Radio Future, Tork: Prehistoric Punk); the other 30 (including the 23 just shuffled, plus ToeJam & Earl III, Gunvalkyrie, Halo: Combat Evolved, Panzer Dragoon Orta, NBA Live 2004, Call of Duty 3, Capcom vs. SNK 2 EO) have no route in this tree and run as a soak to the title screen with --frames-every.
